questions.stem: The owner of Kestrel Kitchenware paid her family's home electricity bill from the business bank account and the payment was recorded as Drawings. Which accounting assumption has been applied?
options: the period assumption
the accrual basis assumption
the accounting entity assumption
the going concern assumption
questions.explanation: The entity assumption keeps the owner's private affairs separate from the business, so a private bill paid with business cash is a withdrawal by the owner, not a business expense. The accrual basis assumption is about when revenue and expenses are recognised, not whose transaction it is.

questions.stem: Kestrel Kitchenware keeps every invoice, receipt and EFT record it uses to prepare its General Journal entries. Which qualitative characteristic does this most directly support?
options: timeliness
comparability
understandability
verifiability
questions.explanation: Verifiability means independent observers can confirm that a transaction has been faithfully recorded, and it is maintained by keeping the source documents and checking them through audit. Comparability is about being able to compare information across periods or entities, which keeping documents does not itself achieve.

questions.stem: The owner of Banksia Bike Supplies wants to record a cash contribution of capital as Sales so that profit looks stronger in a bank loan application. Which qualitative characteristic would this breach most directly?
options: faithful representation, because the report would no longer be neutral and free from error
timeliness, because the loan application would rely on information prepared too late
comparability, because the report would use a different format from other businesses
understandability, because the bank would not have enough knowledge to read the report
questions.explanation: A capital contribution is not revenue, so recording it as Sales would make the Income Statement biased and materially wrong, breaching faithful representation. The problem is not the format or the timing of the report but that it misstates what happened.

questions.stem: A supplier sends a document to a trading business confirming that the amount it owes has been reduced because damaged goods were returned. This document is a:
options: purchase invoice
delivery docket
credit note
statement of account
questions.explanation: A credit note is issued by the seller to reduce the amount the customer owes, usually after a return or an overcharge. A statement of account summarises all invoices, returns and payments over a period rather than recording one return.

questions.stem: Which source document would usually support the General Journal entry when the owner takes inventory from the shop for personal use?
options: a cash receipt
a sales invoice
a purchase invoice
a memo
questions.explanation: The owner taking inventory is an internal transaction with no outside party, so it is supported by a memo prepared within the business. A sales invoice records a sale to a customer, and no sale occurs when the owner takes goods.

questions.stem: At the end of the month, Lin's Lighting receives a document from its supplier listing the opening balance owed, each invoice, a return and a payment, and the closing balance owed. This document is a:
options: purchase order
bank statement
statement of account
credit note
questions.explanation: A statement of account summarises the transactions between a supplier and a customer for a period and shows the balance owing. A credit note records a single reduction in the amount owed, not the whole month's activity.

questions.stem: A liability is best defined as:
options: the residual interest in the assets of the entity after all obligations are deducted
a present obligation of the entity to transfer an economic resource as a result of past events
a future obligation of the entity that may arise if certain expected events occur later
a decrease in assets that results in a decrease in owner's equity during the period
questions.explanation: The study design defines a liability as a present obligation to transfer an economic resource as a result of past events. A decrease in assets that reduces owner's equity describes an expense, and the residual interest describes owner's equity.

questions.stem: Which transaction increases owner's equity but is NOT revenue?
options: A supplier allows a discount for prompt payment.
Inventory is sold for cash above its cost price.
The owner contributes her own van to the business.
An inventory gain is found at the annual stocktake.
questions.explanation: Revenues increase owner's equity other than through contributions from the owner, so a contribution of a van is capital, not revenue. An inventory gain, a discount received and a sale above cost all increase equity through the ordinary activities of the business, so they are revenue.

questions.stem: Which item would be classified as a non-current asset of a trading business?
options: inventory expected to be sold within three months
accounts receivable due for payment within 30 days
a GST refund due from the Australian Taxation Office
shop fittings expected to be used for six years
questions.explanation: Non-current assets are used by the business for a number of years and are not held for resale, which describes shop fittings. Inventory is a current asset even though the business keeps holding inventory, because each item is expected to be sold within 12 months.

questions.stem: Banksia Bike Supplies has a $60,000 loan, of which $12,000 of principal is repayable in the next 12 months. How should the loan be reported in the Balance Sheet?
options: $60,000 as a non-current liability, because the loan runs for several years
$60,000 as a current liability, because repayments have already begun
$48,000 as a current liability and $12,000 as a non-current liability
$12,000 as a current liability and $48,000 as a non-current liability
questions.explanation: Only the principal that must be repaid within 12 months of the end of the reporting period is a current liability; the rest of the loan is non-current. Reporting the whole loan as non-current understates the obligations the business must meet in the coming year.

questions.stem: At the end of the reporting period the GST Clearing account of Lin's Lighting has a credit balance of $3,200. This balance is:
options: a current liability, owed to the Australian Taxation Office
a current asset, a refund due from the Australian Taxation Office
a revenue, because it was collected from customers on sales
a non-current liability, because GST is settled once a year
questions.explanation: A credit balance in GST Clearing means more GST has been collected on sales than paid on purchases, so the business owes the difference to the ATO, normally within a few months. A debit balance would represent a refund due, a current asset; GST collected is never revenue because it belongs to the ATO.

questions.stem: Kestrel Kitchenware sells inventory on credit for $2,200 including GST. The inventory cost $1,200. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
options: Assets +$1,000; Liabilities nil; Owner's equity +$1,000
Assets +$2,200; Liabilities nil; Owner's equity +$2,200
Assets +$1,000; Liabilities +$200; Owner's equity +$800
Assets +$2,200; Liabilities +$200; Owner's equity +$2,000
questions.explanation: Accounts Receivable rises by $2,200 and Inventory falls by $1,200, a net $1,000 increase in assets; GST Clearing rises by $200; and owner's equity rises by the $800 profit on the sale (Sales $2,000 less Cost of Goods Sold $1,200). Leaving out the cost of the inventory sold overstates both assets and equity by $1,200.

questions.stem: The owner of Kestrel Kitchenware takes home inventory that cost the business $300. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
options: Assets nil; Liabilities +$300; Owner's equity −$300
Assets −$300; Liabilities nil; Owner's equity −$300
Assets −$330; Liabilities −$30; Owner's equity −$300
Assets −$300; Liabilities −$30; Owner's equity −$270
questions.explanation: Drawings of inventory are recorded at cost with GST excluded, so Inventory falls by $300 and owner's equity falls by $300 through Drawings. Adding GST to the drawing is wrong because the study design excludes GST from drawings of inventory.

questions.stem: Lin's Lighting owes a supplier $4,400. It pays $4,300 by EFT and is allowed a $100 settlement discount for paying early. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
options: Assets −$4,300; Liabilities −$4,200; Owner's equity −$100
Assets −$4,300; Liabilities −$4,400; Owner's equity +$100
Assets −$4,400; Liabilities −$4,400; Owner's equity nil
Assets −$4,300; Liabilities −$4,300; Owner's equity nil
questions.explanation: Bank falls by the $4,300 paid while the whole $4,400 debt is extinguished, and the $100 difference is Discount Revenue, which increases owner's equity. Treating the payment as if only $4,300 of the debt were cleared ignores the discount and would leave $100 still owing.

questions.stem: The owner of Banksia Bike Supplies contributes a utility vehicle with a fair value of $15,000, and the business also takes over the $6,000 loan still owing on it. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
options: Assets +$9,000; Liabilities nil; Owner's equity +$9,000
Assets +$15,000; Liabilities +$6,000; Owner's equity +$21,000
Assets +$15,000; Liabilities +$6,000; Owner's equity +$9,000
Assets +$15,000; Liabilities nil; Owner's equity +$15,000
questions.explanation: The vehicle is recorded at its fair value of $15,000, the loan taken over is a $6,000 liability, and the owner's capital rises only by the net $9,000 she has contributed. Crediting Capital with the full $15,000 ignores the obligation the business has taken on.

questions.stem: In a T-form General Ledger account, the cross-reference beside each amount shows:
options: the amount of GST that is included in the entry
the name of the account affected by the other side of the entry
the number of the source document that supports the entry
the running balance of the account after the entry is posted
questions.explanation: Each entry in a T-form account shows the date, the cross-reference to the other account in the double entry, and the amount. Source document numbers belong in the General Journal narration, and a T-form account has no running balance column.

questions.stem: The narration in a General Journal entry provides:
options: the closing balance of each General Ledger account affected
the total of the debit and credit columns for the period
the classification of each account as current or non-current
a brief explanation of the transaction and its source document
questions.explanation: Each General Journal entry is followed by a short narration explaining the transaction and naming the document it comes from, which supports verifiability. Balances and totals are found in the ledger and the Trial Balance, not in the narration.

questions.stem: Ning Wu sets up a double entry system for her shop with these balances: Bank $8,000; Inventory $22,000; Shop fittings $15,000; Accounts payable $6,000; Loan $10,000. What amount is credited to Capital in the opening General Journal entry?
questions.explanation: Capital is the balancing figure: assets of $45,000 less liabilities of $16,000 gives $29,000. Deducting only Accounts payable gives $39,000, which leaves out the loan, and $45,000 is total assets with no liabilities deducted.

questions.stem: Kestrel Kitchenware sells inventory on credit for $3,300 including GST; the inventory cost $1,800. Which accounts are credited?
options: Accounts Receivable $3,300 and Inventory $1,800
Sales $3,000, GST Clearing $300 and Inventory $1,800
Sales $3,300 and Inventory $1,800
Sales $3,000, GST Clearing $300 and Cost of Goods Sold $1,800
questions.explanation: Under the perpetual method a credit sale needs two entries: Accounts Receivable is debited $3,300 with Sales and GST Clearing credited, and Cost of Goods Sold is debited $1,800 with Inventory credited. Cost of Goods Sold is an expense that increases, so it is debited, not credited.

questions.stem: A customer returns goods originally sold on credit to Lin's Lighting for $440 including GST. Which account is debited with $400?
options: Sales
Accounts Receivable
Cost of Goods Sold
Sales Returns
questions.explanation: A sales return is recorded by debiting Sales Returns $400 and GST Clearing $40 and crediting Accounts Receivable $440, with a second entry returning the goods to Inventory at cost. Sales itself is not debited because the study design keeps returns in a separate account, which closes with the revenues.

questions.stem: Banksia Bike Supplies returns faulty goods to a supplier and receives a credit note for $660 including GST. How is GST Clearing affected?
options: debited $60
credited $66
debited $66
credited $60
questions.explanation: The return reverses part of the original purchase: Accounts Payable is debited $660, Inventory is credited $600 and GST Clearing is credited $60, cancelling the GST originally claimed. Debiting GST Clearing would increase the GST claimed, which is the opposite of what a return does.

questions.stem: A customer owing Kestrel Kitchenware $2,200 pays within the discount period and is allowed a 2% settlement discount. GST on settlement discounts is excluded. Which General Journal entry records the receipt?
options: Dr Bank 2,156; Dr Discount Expense 40; Dr GST Clearing 4; Cr Accounts Receivable 2,200
Dr Bank 2,200; Cr Discount Revenue 44; Cr Accounts Receivable 2,156
Dr Bank 2,156; Cr Accounts Receivable 2,156
Dr Bank 2,156; Dr Discount Expense 44; Cr Accounts Receivable 2,200
questions.explanation: The discount is 2% of $2,200, or $44, so $2,156 is banked, the $44 is Discount Expense, and the whole $2,200 debt is cleared. Splitting out GST is wrong because the study design excludes GST on settlement discounts, and crediting only $2,156 would leave $44 still owing.

questions.stem: Lin's Lighting pays a supplier early and is allowed a settlement discount of $22. How is the $22 recorded?
options: as an increase in Capital, like an owner's contribution
as a debit to GST Clearing, which reduces the GST owed
as Discount Revenue, which increases net profit
as Discount Expense, which decreases net profit
questions.explanation: A discount received for prompt payment is Discount Revenue, so it increases net profit. Discount Expense is the discount the business allows to its own customers, and GST on settlement discounts is excluded under the study design.

questions.stem: Banksia Bike Supplies pays $4,950 including GST by EFT for a radio advertising campaign. What amount is debited to GST Clearing?
questions.explanation: GST is one-eleventh of a GST-inclusive amount, so $4,950 ÷ 11 = $450, and Advertising is debited $4,500. Taking 10% of the inclusive price gives $495, which overstates the GST because 10% applies to the price before GST.

questions.stem: Inventory taken from the shelves to use in a shop window advertising display is recorded by:
options: debiting Inventory and crediting Advertising at cost price
debiting Advertising and crediting Inventory at cost price
debiting Advertising and crediting Sales at selling price
debiting Drawings and crediting Inventory at cost price
questions.explanation: Inventory used for advertising becomes an Advertising expense at its cost, with GST excluded under the study design. No sale has taken place, so Sales is not credited, and Drawings is used only when the owner takes goods for private use.

questions.stem: The owner of Lin's Lighting takes a lamp home for her lounge room. The lamp cost $180 and sells for $300. Which entry is recorded?
options: Dr Drawings 300; Cr Inventory 180; Cr Sales 120
Dr Drawings 180; Cr Inventory 180
Dr Drawings 300; Cr Sales 300
Dr Drawings 198; Cr Inventory 180; Cr GST Clearing 18
questions.explanation: Drawings of inventory are recorded at cost, with GST excluded, so Drawings is debited $180 and Inventory credited $180. Using the selling price treats the drawing as a sale, but the owner taking goods earns the business no revenue.

questions.stem: The owner of Banksia Bike Supplies contributes a trailer she bought privately for $9,000 three years ago. Its fair value is now $5,500. Which entry is recorded?
options: Dr Trailer 5,500; Cr Capital 5,500
Dr Trailer 9,000; Cr Capital 9,000
Dr Trailer 5,500; Cr Loan 5,500
Dr Capital 5,500; Cr Trailer 5,500
questions.explanation: A non-current asset contributed by the owner is recorded at its fair value, with Capital credited because the owner's investment has increased. The original private cost of $9,000 is not relevant to the business, and the business owes the owner nothing, so no loan arises.

questions.stem: A stocktake at Kestrel Kitchenware reveals more inventory on hand than the inventory cards show. Which entry records this?
options: Dr Inventory; Cr Cost of Goods Sold
Dr Inventory; Cr Capital
Dr Inventory; Cr Inventory Gain
Dr Inventory Loss; Cr Inventory
questions.explanation: When the count exceeds the records, Inventory is increased and the difference is recorded as Inventory Gain, a revenue. An inventory loss is the opposite situation, where the count is below the records.

questions.stem: Which entry records the payment of the balance owing to the Australian Taxation Office on GST Clearing?
options: Dr GST Expense; Cr Bank
Dr GST Clearing; Cr Sales
Dr GST Clearing; Cr Bank
Dr Bank; Cr GST Clearing
questions.explanation: A credit balance in GST Clearing is a liability, so paying it reduces the liability with a debit and reduces Bank with a credit. GST is not an expense of the business, which only collects and passes it on.

questions.stem: GST Clearing at Lin's Lighting opens the month with a credit balance of $1,200. During the month: credit sales $22,000 and credit purchases $13,200 (both including GST), and a purchase return of $1,100 including GST. What is the closing balance?
options: $3,300 credit
$2,100 credit
$1,900 credit
$900 credit
questions.explanation: GST collected on sales of $2,000 is credited, GST paid on purchases of $1,200 is debited, and the purchase return credits back $100: 1,200 + 2,000 − 1,200 + 100 = $2,100 credit. Treating the return as another debit gives $1,900, and leaving out the opening balance gives $900.

questions.stem: A payment of $440 including GST for repairs to the delivery van was debited in error to the Vehicle account; GST was recorded correctly. Which entry corrects the error?
options: Dr Repairs 400; Dr GST Clearing 40; Cr Vehicle 440
Dr Repairs 400; Cr Vehicle 400
Dr Vehicle 400; Cr Repairs 400
Dr Repairs 440; Cr Vehicle 440
questions.explanation: Only $400 went to the wrong account, so the correction moves $400 from Vehicle to Repairs, leaving the correctly recorded $40 of GST alone. Reversing $440 would remove GST that was never in the Vehicle account.

questions.stem: Banksia Bike Supplies paid rent of $1,100 including GST, but the whole $1,100 was debited to Rent Expense. If this is not corrected, what is the effect on the reports?
options: Net profit is understated by $100 and the GST liability is overstated by $100
Net profit is overstated by $100 and the GST liability is understated by $100
Net profit is understated by $1,100 and Bank is overstated by $1,100
Net profit is correct but the GST liability is overstated by $100
questions.explanation: Rent Expense is $100 too high, so profit is $100 too low, and the $100 of GST paid was never debited to GST Clearing, so the amount shown as owing to the ATO is $100 too high. Bank is correct because the $1,100 payment was credited properly.

questions.stem: Which General Journal entry corrects the rent error, where $1,100 including GST was all debited to Rent Expense?
options: Dr GST Clearing 110; Cr Rent Expense 110
Dr GST Clearing 100; Cr Bank 100
Dr GST Clearing 100; Cr Rent Expense 100
Dr Rent Expense 100; Cr GST Clearing 100
questions.explanation: The $100 of GST was wrongly included in Rent Expense, so it is moved out of the expense and into GST Clearing. Crediting Bank would record a second payment that never happened.

questions.stem: The main purpose of a Trial Balance is to:
options: check that total debit balances equal total credit balances in the ledger
show the profit earned by the business for the reporting period
report the financial position of the business at the end of the period
prove that every transaction has been recorded in the correct account
questions.explanation: A Trial Balance lists every General Ledger balance and checks the arithmetical accuracy of the double entry. It cannot prove each transaction is in the right account, because some errors leave debits and credits equal.

questions.stem: Which error would NOT be revealed by the Trial Balance of Kestrel Kitchenware?
options: The credit side of a cash payment was posted to Bank twice.
A credit purchase of inventory for $1,100 was not recorded at all.
A credit sale was posted to Accounts Receivable but not to Sales.
A $540 debit to Wages was posted to the ledger as $450.
questions.explanation: If a transaction is omitted completely, debits and credits both fall short by the same amount and the Trial Balance still balances. Each of the other errors affects only one side of the ledger, so the totals would disagree.

questions.stem: Which account normally has a credit balance in the Trial Balance of a trading business?
options: Drawings
Discount Revenue
Discount Expense
Sales Returns
questions.explanation: Revenue accounts normally have credit balances, so Discount Revenue is the credit. Sales Returns reduces revenue and Drawings reduces owner's equity, so both normally have debit balances.

questions.stem: Which internal control procedure is an example of the separation of duties?
options: Cash on hand is banked intact at the end of every trading day.
The employee who receives cash does not also record it in the ledger.
Every cash receipt is pre-numbered and issued in numerical order.
Inventory is counted at least once a year and compared with records.
questions.explanation: Separating duties means no single employee controls a transaction from start to finish, so taking cash and recording it are given to different people. Pre-numbered receipts and regular banking are also internal controls, but they are not separation of duties.

questions.stem: Inventory at Lin's Lighting keeps going missing without explanation. Which internal control would most directly detect this?
options: regular physical counts compared with the inventory card balances
issuing pre-numbered sales invoices for every credit sale
requiring two signatures on every EFT payment to suppliers
sending statements of account to every customer each month
questions.explanation: Comparing physical counts with the balances on the inventory cards reveals any shortfall, which can then be investigated and recorded as an inventory loss. Payment signatures and customer statements protect cash and receivables, not goods on the shelves.

questions.stem: A bookkeeper at Banksia Bike Supplies sets up a fake supplier and pays its invoices into her own bank account. Which control would most effectively prevent this fraud?
options: Payments need a matched purchase order and invoice, approved by a second person.
All invoices are recorded in the General Journal on the day they are received.
The business pays every supplier within its credit terms to earn discounts.
The bookkeeper prepares a monthly Trial Balance for the owner to review.
questions.explanation: Requiring an approved purchase order to match each invoice, and a second person to authorise payment, stops one employee from creating and paying a false liability. A balanced Trial Balance would not reveal the fraud because the false entries are recorded with equal debits and credits.

questions.stem: The owner of Kestrel Kitchenware asks the bookkeeper to record her family holiday as a business travel expense. Apart from breaching the entity assumption, what is the main ethical problem?
options: Profit would be overstated, so the owner would pay more tax than she owes.
Assets would be overstated, so the bank would lend more than it should.
Liabilities would be understated, so suppliers would offer longer credit.
Profit would be understated, so the business would pay less tax than it should.
questions.explanation: Recording a private cost as a business expense understates profit and therefore taxable income, which is dishonest and unlawful. The holiday was paid in cash, so it reduces assets either way; the issue is that the expense is fictitious.

questions.stem: Lin's Lighting can buy LED globes from a cheap overseas supplier with a poor record on worker safety, or from a dearer local supplier. Which statement best describes the decision?
options: It weighs a financial benefit against a social consideration for the supplier's workers.
It is purely financial, because the owner's only obligation is to maximise profit.
It is an environmental consideration only, because the globes are energy efficient.
It is decided by the accrual basis assumption, which requires the cheapest supplier.
questions.explanation: Choosing a supplier affects cost and therefore profit, but it also has a social dimension in the treatment of the workers who make the goods. No accounting assumption requires the cheapest supplier, and treating the choice as purely financial ignores the ethical considerations the study design asks owners to weigh.

questions.stem: Kestrel Kitchenware buys inventory for cash for $990 including GST. Which entry records this purchase?
options: Dr Inventory 900; Dr GST Clearing 90; Cr Bank 990
Dr Inventory 990; Cr Bank 990
Dr Inventory 900; Cr GST Clearing 90; Cr Bank 810
Dr Cost of Goods Sold 900; Dr GST Clearing 90; Cr Bank 990
questions.explanation: Under the perpetual method purchases go straight to the Inventory asset at cost excluding GST, and the GST paid is debited to GST Clearing because it can be claimed back. Cost of Goods Sold is recorded only when the inventory is later sold.
